People tab mock-up

M1 slice S4 adds three things: a tab bar with Town and People; the People tab, a list of everyone in Ashwick that you can filter and sort; and a sheet for each resident, with their skills, traits and morale, and a way to pin them to a job.

These are screenshots of the real app at 412 px, then 360 px, running a working prototype of S4. The town is seed 1's eight real founders. Every number is what the prototype's engine produced from the state named in each section; where I set a starting value by hand, the section says so. Nothing here is merged; it waits for your answer.

The same prototype also turns on what S4 changes underneath: skill now grows with work (1 point per 3 game days in one job), morale moves each game day toward its reasons, and a worker's output now follows their skill and morale. Seed 1's four foragers made 45 food over their first 4 game days, where S3 gave 48 (measured).

A. The People tab

Day 2, after the first day's morale was weighed. Each row shows the name, the people, the trade (or "No trade" in ember, because no work costs morale) and the highest skill. Morale sits on the right: ember under 30, moss from 70. The chips filter; there is one chip per trade that someone has. Sort is by name to start with.

Filtered to Idle

Idle shows the four with no job. No separate "No trade" chip, since it would be the same list.

B. A resident's sheet

Ceriin has no work. The sheet opens on Work, then Morale with each reason and its number, then Skills and Traits. Traits say which buildings they like and dislike.

C. Pin to…

Mairoc forages. "Pin to…" lists every built workplace with what that work would do to their morale, read from the engine, and its workers. Here the town started with its wood set to 100 by hand, so a Mine could be built at once (40 wood, 1 game day); the engine then ran a game day, leaving 60 wood. Mairoc is Sociable, which dislikes a Mine.

Pinning asks first

Choosing the Mine shows the cost before anything is sent: each reason, then the total from this work. Nothing changes until you tap Pin.

After pinning

Pinned residents are placed first, so Mairoc moves to the Mine at once and Ceriin, the Mine's weakest miner (mining 23), moves to the hut. The sheet shows the job and the pin; Unpin takes it back.

D. Three game days later

The town is fed with food to spare (+10), but Mairoc dislikes the work (−10), so his morale heads for 50 and has fallen from 55 to 50. His mining rose by 1 from 3 days' work.

E. A hungry town (alert state)

Set by hand: everyone at morale 30 and food at 0 just before a day starts. The day finds no food, so the town is not fed (−30) and every morale drops by 5 to 25, in ember. Sorted by morale, lowest first, so trouble comes to the top.

F. A new town (empty state)

Before the first game day no reasons exist yet, so the sheet says when morale is weighed instead of an empty list.

G. At 360 px

Nothing scrolls sideways; the chips wrap if there are more trades.

Loading

Unchanged: "Loading…" until the town arrives, as on the Town tab.

Choices drawn here that the spec left open

  • The tab bar shows Town and People only. The Town tab keeps the Save and app block at its foot. The chosen tab is not kept over a reload.
  • The sheet's order is Work (job, pin, Pin to…), Morale, Skills, Traits, because the choice you make on it is the pin; the spec lists skills and traits first.
  • "Pin to…" is a plain button, since it only opens the list; the amber is kept for Pin, which changes the town.
  • A row shows name, people, trade, highest skill and morale. "Pinned" is added to the row of a pinned resident.
  • Sort: Name (A to Z, the default), Morale (lowest first), Top skill (highest first). Ties go by name.
  • Morale colour on screen: ember under 30, moss from 70. These are display only; the rules use their own numbers (leaving is below 15, in S5).
  • Reasons with a value of 0 are not listed (for example Food when there is between 1 and 2 food a head after eating). The tavern reason starts in S5.
  • "Pin to…" lists every built workplace, the one they are pinned to marked "Pinned here now" and off. The confirm shows each reason and the total "From this work". A workplace with no open slots warns that they will not work there until one opens.
  • An Unpin button, which the spec did not list; the engine already accepts it.
  • When a pin cannot be met (more pinned residents than open slots), the sheet says "No free slot at the Mine: works elsewhere until one opens." D-013 says a pinned resident complies; in the rules they comply whenever a slot is open.
  • The sheet's first line is "A human, 20 years old". Every settler is 20 until families come in M4a (spec, an assumption).
  • Skill and morale now change output, so the tests that pinned seed 1's food at a flat 100% now use residents at skill 50 and morale 50, or read the new numbers from the engine.

  • Fresh check (one reviewer agent, 75,038 tokens measured): 1 major, 2 unverified, 5 minor. Fixed: the page now says where a starting value was set by hand (the wood for the Mine, the hungry town); "Pin to…" is a plain button, so only Pin carries amber; the sheet's order is listed as a choice. Confirmed and left: 45 and 48 food (content.test.ts reads 45; S3's 48); the two no-slot warnings are worded on the page but not screenshotted, since they need more pins than slots. Declined: the tab bar's line is --head, not amber; the amber chevron is the Town tab's own pattern for a row that opens a sheet.
